paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. David is in real danger, with men watching his house to kill him (Psalm 59:1), and he doesn't pretend he's fine. He says it plainly to God: "Deliver me from my enemies, O my God." The first thing he does with his fear is pray it out loud.

But look at where the song lands. By the end, David calls God his "fortress" and his "refuge in times of trouble" (Psalm 59:16). He says "I will keep watch for You, O my strength" (Psalm 59:9), and he says God "will come to meet me" (Psalm 59:10). The enemies are still out there, and David still sings. His trust doesn't wait for the trouble to leave.

So when your own evening comes, baker, and something is snarling and prowling around your city, you can do what David did. Tell God what's happening, the whole thing, no editing. Then sing of His strength and His loving devotion in the morning (Psalm 59:16), because He is your fortress when the night is long. I spent years in the dark without a hum, so trust me, singing is better. This is a psalm, a song straight from the heart, and that's why I picked it for you.
